## Setup

**Goal:** turn a meeting transcript into a retrospective with the themes already queued in the parking lot.

1. Copy the **Webhook** node's Production URL and register it with your transcript tool (Zoom / Fathom / Grain / Otter all support outgoing webhooks). The workflow expects `body.transcript` (plain text) — add a mapping step in your tool if its payload differs.
2. Add your AI provider credential on **Extract Themes**.
3. On **Create Retrospective**: pick your TeamRetro credential and paste your **team ID**. It uses your team's last-used template (`useLastTemplate`).
4. **Activate**.

**How it works:** the AI returns themes tagged *went-well* / *needs-improvement*, prefixed 👍 / 🔧, and each is parked for the team. The facilitator pulls the relevant ones onto the board when the session starts — AI seeds it, humans run it.

**Why the parking lot, not idea cards?** Writing an idea into an *open* retro is a per-person act, so the API requires a user token (OAuth). n8n authenticates with an API key (`trt_`/`tra_`), so idea capture returns `403`. Parked items are the API-key path. Needs the **parking lot** plan feature — a `403` on **Park Theme** means it's off.

values.content: You extract retrospective themes from meeting transcripts. Return STRICT JSON: {"themes":[{"title":"...","sentiment":"went-well"|"needs-improvement"}]}. 4-8 themes, each title under 100 characters, written as a team observation (e.g. "Deploy pipeline failed twice during release week"). No commentary.
